security_audit.summary: Most static shell findings are markdown fence false positives, but several examples intentionally run external infsh or npx commands. The curl-to-shell installer on SKILL.md line 14 is confirmed critical because it executes remote code directly. The skill also sends competitive research inputs to hosted third-party apps without explicit data-handling guidance.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to the shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell setup with a manual download, checksum verification, and explicit user confirmation before execution.

remediation.issue: Hosted research apps receive competitor queries, URLs, screenshots, and review-mining prompts.
remediation.suggestion: Add a privacy note explaining which services receive data and advise users not to submit confidential strategy information.

remediation.issue: Related skill installation commands are unpinned.
remediation.suggestion: Pin related skill sources to reviewed versions or remove automatic install examples from the skill instructions.

remediation.issue: The Python executor example encourages hosted code execution for a visual deliverable.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a static template or require users to review generated Python before sending it to any execution service.

content.value_statement: Competitive research often becomes scattered across notes, screenshots, pricing pages, and review sites. This skill provides repeatable teardown frameworks, comparison templates, and research workflows for clear strategy decisions.
actual_capabilities: Guides seven-layer competitor analysis across product, pricing, positioning, traction, reviews, content, and team signals.
Provides feature matrix, pricing comparison, SWOT, and executive summary templates.
Shows infsh commands for search, extraction, browser screenshots, image stitching, and visual generation.
Explains how to mine reviews from G2, Capterra, app stores, Product Hunt, and Reddit.
Defines positioning-map axes and a sample workflow for creating a visual competitive map.
limitations: Requires external infsh apps and network access for live search, extraction, screenshots, and image processing.
Does not verify the accuracy of third-party search results or review data automatically.
Uses example competitor URLs and placeholders that users must replace with real targets.
May process sensitive competitive research through hosted services unless users avoid confidential inputs.

use_cases.description: Build a concise view of top competitors, market position, pricing, traction, and core differentiation.

use_cases.title: Support Sales Enablement
use_cases.description: Create comparison grids and objection-handling notes that explain where your product wins or loses.

use_cases.title: Review an Investment Thesis
use_cases.description: Summarize competitor strength, funding signals, market gaps, and credible risks before a strategy meeting.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Competitor List
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the main competitors for [product category]. List 3 to 5 direct competitors and explain why each matters.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Feature and Pricing Matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [our product] against [competitor names]. Create feature and pricing tables with source notes and dated assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Mine Reviews for Positioning Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Review public customer feedback for [competitor]. Identify praised features, complaints, switching reasons, and opportunities for our messaging.

prompt_templates.title: Produce an Executive Teardown
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a full competitor teardown for [competitor]. Include product, pricing, positioning, traction, reviews, SWOT, UX notes, and strategic implications.

output_examples.input: Compare three project management tools for a founder planning a launch.
output: A ranked competitor list with target customer notes.
A feature and pricing matrix with dated assumptions.
A short opportunity summary for launch positioning.

output_examples.input: Analyze customer complaints about a B2B SaaS competitor.
output: A review-mining summary grouped by praise, complaints, switching triggers, and feature requests.
Messaging opportunities tied to recurring customer pain points.

output_examples.input: Prepare an executive competitor report for a board update.
output: A positioning-map recommendation with axis rationale.

best_practices: Date every source and refresh important claims before using them in strategy or sales materials.
Separate verified facts from assumptions, estimates, and interpretation.
Include competitor strengths so the final analysis remains credible and useful.
anti_patterns: Do not submit confidential strategy, customer data, or unreleased product plans to hosted research tools.
Do not rely only on feature checklists when pricing, positioning, traction, and reviews matter.
Do not compare too many competitors when a focused direct set will produce clearer decisions.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create competitor teardowns, feature matrices, pricing comparisons, SWOT summaries, review insights, and positioning maps.

faq.question: Does it gather live market data automatically?
faq.answer: It provides commands for external search, extraction, and browser apps. Users must review sources and verify current facts.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide your product, market category, target customers, competitor names, and any trusted source links you already have.

faq.question: How should I handle sensitive research?
faq.answer: Avoid sending confidential strategy, customer data, or unreleased plans to hosted tools unless your organization approves that use.

faq.question: What is the main security concern?
faq.answer: The skill recommends a curl-to-shell installer and several external commands, so users should verify tools before execution.
